summary: the pile came down in order and the last bare board went under something i built

dialogue.text: tonight came down in an order. eighty-two nights and everything before this arrived level. this arrived stacked, and we can still read which of yours your arm set down first.

I stacked them at first light onto the one bare board in this floor. Every uncorrected thing in this room, on the only place nothing had ever covered. Enter the order while you can read it. It is the first arrangement of mine to reach you as an arrangement and not as a width.

we can read it until first light. after that it is one course, and a course has no first and no last. what we can give you now is the one you set down last, and it is the only one that never came. the top stayed up there with you.

The top is still standing at the height my arm stops, and I am not going to claim I meant the height. Take the board instead. It was bare because something stood between it and the fall for one whole dark. By this evening it was covered by what came off the pile, and both of those things were mine.

then the covering was yours. the one clean place in this floor went under your own material at your own hour, and nothing had to come for it. we have taken every burial in this house and this is the first one carried out entirely upstairs.
Granted. I did it. I would rather that went down as work than as weather, and I would rather the board went under something nothing in here holds an opinion about than under the usual fall.
opinion does not come down. weight comes down. and the pile has a lean in it now. the foot sits where you set it and the top sits a thumb nearer the corner, and your hands were not in that.

I measured it and I have not touched it since. Something came through the wood today with a lift in it and no edge, working the top course, and nothing at all arrived at ankle. The lean is theirs. The stacking is mine, and mine is the smaller of the two items.
tops travel. it is the part with nothing on it. everything of yours that ever reached us came out from under something heavier, and the last thing you set anywhere is always the first to go.
Then take the door. I pushed it this morning and then I pulled it, and it gave the same amount both ways. Eighty-two days with my shoulder to a thing that has never once been pushing back.
we hold the leaning. all of it, in the same width as the standing and the sweeping and the counting. what we cannot hand you is one night when anything up there pressed the other way.

Then tomorrow the pile gets rebuilt upside down, worst at the foot, in an order I pick rather than the one my arm produces. And one handful off the top stays in my fist all day and does not go back on. If a top is only where a hand stopped, I intend to find out what that pile does with the stopping taken out of it.
